mainTopic: דניאל compared with חגי, זכריה and מלאכי; the hidden fear sensed by one's מזל and its remedies; and the closed ם in לםרבה, which hints that חזקיהו was meant to be the משיח
overview: The amud opens by comparing דניאל with חגי, זכריה and מלאכי. They were נביאים, but only דניאל saw the vision. רבינא learns from their fear that when a person is frightened for no visible reason, his מזל has sensed something, and the גמרא gives remedies. Next, בר קפרא explains the closed ם in לםרבה: הקב״ה wanted to make חזקיהו the משיח, but מדת הדין objected because חזקיהו did not sing praise after his miracles. The earth sang in his place, but a בת קול answered 'My secret is Mine,' and the redemption was put off. The גמרא adds teachings about waiting through the night of exile, about the disgrace of not singing praise (חזקיהו, and משה with יתרו), and about the word ויחד. It then expounds ישעיהו 10:16: חזקיהו and סנחריב each had eight names. It also explains why סנחריב was honored for not speaking badly of ארץ ישראל, while the exiles did speak badly of it. Finally, it discusses how סנחריב's army was burned and begins comparing סנחריב with פרעה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Who was greater: דניאל or the three prophets?
steps.stepSummary: חגי, זכריה and מלאכי were greater than דניאל because they were נביאים. דניאל was greater than them because he saw the vision and they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They (חגי, זכריה, מלאכי) were greater than him (דניאל), and he was greater than them. They were greater because they were prophets and he was not. He was greater because he saw the vision and they did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares דניאל with the three men who were with him during his vision, and shows that each side had its own advantage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דניאל says only דניאל saw the vision, while the men with him did not. Being a נביא means having a mission to bring ה׳'s message to the people, and דניאל did not have that role. Still, in this one case דניאל saw something they could not see.

phrases.english: They were greater than he,
phrases.notes: "They" means חגי, זכריה and מלאכי, and "he" means דניאל.

phrases.english: and he was greater than they.
They were greater than he —
for they were prophets, and he was not a prophet.
And he was greater than they —
for he saw, and they did not see.
phrases.notes: This is the vision of the angel in דניאל 10:7.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינְהוּ עֲדִיפִי מִינֵּיהּ, וְאִיהוּ עֲדִיף מִנַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion, before this section, that identified the men with דניאל as חגי, זכריה and מלאכי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three prophets were greater in נבואה. דניאל was greater because he saw this vision.

steps.title: If they saw nothing, why were they scared?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the three men were frightened if they did not see the vision.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since they did not see anything, why were they frightened?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem: the פסוק says the men did not see the vision, yet it also says a great fear fell on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fear usually comes from seeing something scary. If they saw nothing, their fear seems to have no cause, so the two parts of the פסוק seem not to fit together.

phrases.english: And since they did not see,
what is the reason they were frightened?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּלָא חֲזוֹ, מַאי טַעְמָא אִיבְּעוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement in step 1 that they did not see.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the three men did not see the vision.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without seeing anything there is no reason for fear, yet the פסוק says they were frightened and fled.

steps.title: Their מזל saw it
steps.stepSummary: The men did not see anything themselves, but their מזל (spiritual guardian) saw the vision. That is why they felt fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though they themselves did not see anything, their guardian angel saw it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: a person's מזל can see what the person cannot, and the person feels the fear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer separates the person from his spiritual side. Their eyes saw nothing, but their מזל saw the angel. That explains both parts of the פסוק: no seeing, but real fear.

keyTerms.meaning: a person's spiritual guardian / heavenly counterpart

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהוּ לָא חֲזוֹ מִידֵּי,
phrases.english: Even though they themselves did not see anything,
their מזל (guardian angel) saw.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהוּ לָא חֲזוֹ מִידֵּי, מַזָּלַיְיהוּ חָזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a new idea: the person and his מזל can perceive separately.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fear must come from something the person himself sees.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מזל can see something and cause the person to feel fear.

steps.title: רבינא: sudden fear means your מזל sees something
steps.stepSummary: רבינא learns a general lesson. When a person suddenly feels scared without seeing anything, his מזל has sensed something.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Learn from this that when a person becomes frightened, even though he does not see anything, his מזל sees it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא takes the answer about the three prophets and turns it into a rule for every person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of חגי, זכריה and מלאכי becomes a model. Unexplained fear is not "nothing"; it is a sign that the person's מזל noticed something dangerous. This sets up the next question about what to do.
steps.whatToRemember: Unexplained fear means one's מזל sensed something unseen. This is learned from the men with דניאל.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Learn from this: a person who becomes frightened,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיהוּ לָא חָזֵי,
phrases.english: even though he does not see,
his מזל sees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson from the answer in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone who feels fear without seeing a cause should know that his מזל sees something.

steps.title: What should a frightened person do?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what remedy there is for someone whose מזל senses danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking for a practical fix for this kind of fear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know the fear points to a real unseen danger, the natural question is how to protect oneself. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: What is his remedy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of רבינא's lesson.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a person should protect himself when he feels sudden fear.

steps.title: Three remedies for sudden fear
steps.stepSummary: He should jump four אמות from his spot, or say קריאת שמע. If he is in a dirty place where he may not say words of Torah, he should say: "The goat in the butcher's house is fatter than me."
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him jump four cubits from his place. Or let him read קריאת שמע. And if he is standing in a filthy place, let him say: "The goat of the slaughterhouse is fatter than I."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives practical ways to escape the unseen danger, including a backup for a place where קריאת שמע is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving four אמות takes the person away from the spot of danger. קריאת שמע gives protection through holy words. In a dirty place, where Torah words are forbidden, he uses a plain sentence that sends the harm toward the fat goat instead of himself.

keyTerms.meaning: the goat of the butcher's house

steps.whatToRemember: Remedies for sudden fear: move four אמות, or say קריאת שמע; in a dirty place, say the goat formula.

phrases.english: Let him leap four cubits from his place.
Alternatively, let him recite קריאת שמע.
And if he is standing in a filthy place,
let him say this:
"The goat of the slaughterhouse is fatter than I."
phrases.notes: He means: go bother that fat goat instead of me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Move four אמות, or recite קריאת שמע; in a filthy place, say the goat formula.

steps.title: Why is there a closed ם in the middle of לםרבה?
steps.stepSummary: Starting a new topic about חזקיהו, the גמרא quotes a פסוק from ישעיהו. בר קפרא asks why the word לםרבה has a closed (final) ם in the middle of the word, when a mem in the middle of a word is always open.
steps.simpleTranslation: "To the increase of the government and to peace there is no end..." רבי תנחום said: בר קפרא taught in ציפורי: Why is every mem in the middle of a word open, but this one is closed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion by pointing out an unusual spelling in a פסוק and asking why it is written that way. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a closed ם appears only at the end of a word. Here it appears inside the word לםרבה, which breaks the normal rule, so בר קפרא looks for a hidden message in it.

keyTerms.meaning: "to increase", written with a closed ם

steps.confusionAlert: The word לםרבה really is written in the ספר with a final ם in the middle. This is not a printing mistake; that unusual spelling is exactly what the question is about.

phrases.english: "To the increase of the government and to peace there is no end, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 9:6.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum said:
Bar Kappara expounded in Tzippori:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה כׇּל מֵם שֶׁבְּאֶמְצַע תֵּיבָה פָּתוּחַ,
phrases.english: Why is every mem in the middle of a word open,
and this one closed?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה כׇּל מֵם שֶׁבְּאֶמְצַע תֵּיבָה פָּתוּחַ, וְזֶה סָתוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about חזקיהו, separate from the discussion of fear.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning behind the closed ם in לםרבה.

steps.title: ה׳ wanted חזקיהו to be the משיח
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא answers that הקב״ה wanted to make חזקיהו the משיח and סנחריב into גוג ומגוג. The closed ם hints at this plan, and step 9 explains why it was closed off.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Holy One, Blessed be He, wanted to make חזקיהו the משיח, and סנחריב into גוג ומגוג.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא begins explaining the closed ם: it connects to ה׳'s plan to bring the final redemption in the time of חזקיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about endless peace and kingship was meant to come true through חזקיהו. סנחריב's war against him would have been the final war of גוג ומגוג. Step 9 explains why the plan was "closed off."

keyTerms.meaning: the enemy nations in the final war before the redemption

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the famous idea that the redemption almost came in חזקיהו's time. The closed ם shows a door to redemption that was closed.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, sought
to make Hezekiah the Messiah,
and Sennacherib Gog and Magog.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּיקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת חִזְקִיָּהוּ מָשִׁיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the שאלה of step 7; step 9 completes the answer by explaining why the plan was closed off (לכך נסתתם).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The closed ם relates to ה׳'s plan to make חזקיהו the משיח and סנחריב into גוג ומגוג.

steps.title: מדת הדין objects to making חזקיהו the משיח
steps.stepSummary: מדת הדין argues that if דוד, who sang many songs, was not made משיח, then חזקיהו, who sang nothing after his miracles, should not be made משיח either. This is why the ם was closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The attribute of justice said to הקב״ה: Master of the World, You did not make דוד king of Israel the משיח, even though he sang many songs and praises to You. Will You make חזקיהו the משיח, when You did all these miracles for him and he did not sing to You? That is why the ם was closed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story from step 8. מדת הדין objects to הקב״ה's plan to make חזקיהו the משיח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is a comparison. דוד sang many praises and still was not made משיח, so חזקיהו, who sang nothing after great miracles, surely should not be. This objection explains the closed ם: the opening for redemption was closed off.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה מִדַּת הַדִּין לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: The attribute of justice said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,
if David, king of Israel,
who said many songs and praises before You,
You did not make him the Messiah,

phrases.aramaic: חִזְקִיָּה שֶׁעָשִׂיתָ לוֹ כׇּל הַנִּסִּים הַלָּלוּ
phrases.english: then Hezekiah, for whom You did all these miracles,
and he did not say a song before You,
will You make him the Messiah?
That is why it was closed.
phrases.notes: "It" is the closed ם in the word לםרבה from step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה מִדַּת הַדִּין לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes בר קפרא's explanation of the closed ם
steps.kashyaTarget: הקב״ה's plan to make חזקיהו the משיח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison from the greater case to the lesser: דוד sang much and was not made משיח, so חזקיהו, who did not sing, should not be made משיח.

steps.title: The earth offers to sing in חזקיהו's place
steps.stepSummary: The ארץ answers the objection by singing praise in place of חזקיהו and asks that he be made משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away the earth spoke up and said to Him: Master of the World, I will sing to You in place of this צדיק, so make him the משיח. It began singing to Him, as the פסוק says: "From the edge of the earth we have heard songs: glory to the righteous."
steps.whatsHappening: The ארץ tries to fix the problem מדת הדין raised. It sings the missing song for חזקיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection was that חזקיהו never sang. The ארץ fills that gap by singing for him, and the פסוק in ישעיהו is read as that song.

phrases.english: Immediately the earth spoke up and said before Him:
Master of the World,
I will say a song before You
in place of this righteous man,
so make him the Messiah.
It began and said a song before Him,
as it is said:
"From the edge of the earth we have heard songs:
glory to the righteous, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 24:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to מדת הדין's objection
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the problem by supplying the missing song
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיהו cannot be משיח because no song was said
steps.terutzMaskana: The ארץ says the song in his place

steps.title: The request is turned down: 'My secret is Mine'
steps.stepSummary: שר העולם asks הקב״ה to fulfill the צדיק's wish, but a בת קול answers "My secret is Mine," so the redemption is not granted now.
steps.simpleTranslation: The angel over the world said to Him: Master of the World, do what this צדיק wants! A heavenly voice came out and said: My secret is Mine, My secret is Mine.
steps.whatsHappening: Another voice joins in asking for חזקיהו to be made משיח, and הקב״ה refuses through a בת קול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word צביונו plays on צבי in the פסוק, and the reply רזי לי is the next phrase of that same פסוק. Its message is that the time of redemption stays hidden, so the plan does not go ahead.

keyTerms.meaning: The angel in charge of the world

phrases.english: The angel of the world said before Him:
Master of the World,
do the wish of this righteous man!
phrases.notes: צביונו sounds like צבי, "glory," in the פסוק just quoted.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said:
My secret is Mine, My secret is Mine.
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק in ישעיהו 24:16.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the attempt to make חזקיהו משיח
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The request to bring the redemption through חזקיהו now
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The time of redemption is הקב״ה's secret

steps.title: The prophet asks how long the exile will last
steps.stepSummary: The נביא cries out and asks how long it will be until the redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: The prophet said: Woe to me, woe to me, until when?
steps.whatsHappening: The נביא reacts to the refusal by asking how long the wait will be. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Woe to me" is also a phrase from the same פסוק. The question looks for a time frame for the exile.

phrases.english: The prophet said:
Woe to me, woe to me,
until when?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר נָבִיא: אוֹי לִי, אוֹי לִי, עַד מָתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the בת קול's refusal
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long the exile will last

steps.title: Until traitors and robbers come
steps.stepSummary: The בת קול answers with the end of the פסוק about traitors, and רבא (or רבי יצחק) explains: until robbers, and robbers of robbers, come.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said: "Traitors have betrayed, and traitors have dealt very treacherously." And רבא, and some say רבי יצחק, said: until robbers come, and robbers of robbers.
steps.whatsHappening: The נביא's question is answered. The redemption will not come until waves of traitors and robbers have passed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the פסוק is read as the answer to "until when?" רבא explains the doubled wording as one group of robbers after another, so the exile will last through several conquering powers.
steps.whatToRemember: חזקיהו could have been משיח, but because he did not sing praise, the redemption was put off. It stays a secret and will come only after a long exile of nation after nation.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said:
"Traitors have betrayed,
and traitors have dealt very treacherously."
And Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yitzchak:
Until robbers come
and robbers of robbers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the נביא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exile lasts until traitors, robbers, and robbers of robbers have come

steps.title: The prophecy about דומה, the angel over the spirits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about דומה, and רבי יוחנן explains that דומה is the name of the angel in charge of the spirits.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The burden of דומה: one calls to me from שעיר: Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?" רבי יוחנן said: The angel appointed over the spirits is named דומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, related פסוק about waiting through the night of exile. רבי יוחנן tells us who דומה is, which sets up the conversation in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The theme stays the same: when will the exile end? רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק as a scene in heaven involving the angel דומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Name of the angel over the spirits

phrases.english: "The burden of Dumah:
one calls to me from Seir:
Watchman, what of the night?
Watchman, what of the night? etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 21:11

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
That angel who is appointed over the spirits,
his name is Dumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related פסוק on the same theme of when the redemption will come
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דומה is the angel in charge of the spirits

steps.title: The spirits ask דומה about the night
steps.stepSummary: All the spirits gather by דומה and ask him what will become of the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the spirits gathered by דומה and said to him: "Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?"
steps.whatsHappening: The spirits ask דומה the words of the פסוק. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Night" stands for the exile. Their question is really: when will this darkness end?

phrases.english: All the spirits gathered by Dumah,
and said to him:
"Watchman, what of the night?
Watchman, what of the night?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Acts out the question in the פסוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When the night of exile will end

steps.title: Morning comes, if you return
steps.stepSummary: דומה answers with the next פסוק: morning and night both come, and if you want it, ask and return.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The watchman said: Morning comes and also night. If you will ask, ask; return, come."
steps.whatsHappening: דומה answers the spirits. The redemption, the morning, is ready to come, but it depends on returning through תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is not a date. It says both morning and night are possible, and the deciding factor is whether people ask and return.
steps.whatToRemember: The redemption is ready to come. It depends on תשובה: if you seek it, return.

phrases.english: "The watchman said:
Morning comes, and also night;
if you will ask, ask;
return, come."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 21:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the spirits' question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Morning (redemption) is available, and it depends on returning in תשובה

steps.title: A disgrace that חזקיה did not sing until the earth sang
steps.stepSummary: רבי פפייס teaches that it was shameful that חזקיה and his followers did not sing to ה׳ after their rescue, so the earth had to sing first.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי פפייס: It is a disgrace for חזקיה and his group that they did not sing, until the earth began and sang, as the פסוק says: 'From the edge of the earth we heard songs: glory to the righteous.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that criticizes חזקיה for not singing שירה after ה׳ saved him from סנחריב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the פסוק 'מכנף הארץ זמרת שמענו'. It shows that the song came from the earth, not from חזקיה. Since the people who were saved should have sung, the earth singing first is described as a גנאי, a disgrace.

keyTerms.meaning: His group, the people around him
A song of praise to ה׳
From the edge of the earth

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of רבי פפייס:
It is a disgrace for חזקיה and his group
that they did not say a song,
until the earth began and said a song,
as it says: 'From the edge of the earth we heard songs,
glory to the righteous, etc.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 24:16. This is the same פסוק the earlier steps were discussing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the opening of the ישעיהו פסוק and draws a lesson about חזקיה from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It was a disgrace that חזקיה and his people did not sing until the earth sang.

steps.title: A similar disgrace: משה and the people waited for יתרו to say ברוך
steps.stepSummary: Using the same pattern, רבי פפייס teaches that משה and the 600,000 should have said ברוך before יתרו did.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a similar way you can say about the פסוק 'And יתרו said: Blessed is ה׳ Who saved you.' It was taught in the name of רבי פפייס: It is a disgrace for משה and the six hundred thousand that they did not say 'Blessed' until יתרו came and said 'Blessed is ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second example of the same idea. Here an outsider, יתרו, praised ה׳ before the people who were actually saved did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase כיוצא בדבר links this case to the case of חזקיה. In both cases the ones who were rescued should have praised ה׳ first. Instead the praise came from someone else: the earth in the first case, and יתרו in this one.

keyTerms.meaning: Blessed, a word used to praise ה׳

phrases.english: In a similar way you say:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיֹּאמֶר יִתְרוֹ בָּרוּךְ ה׳ אֲשֶׁר הִצִּיל אֶתְכֶם״.
phrases.english: 'And יתרו said: Blessed is Hashem Who saved you.'
phrases.notes: שמות 18:10

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of רבי פפייס:
It is a disgrace for משה and the six hundred thousand
that they did not say 'Blessed'
until יתרו came and said 'Blessed is Hashem.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel to step 17, following the same pattern of criticism.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It was a disgrace that משה and Israel did not say ברוך until יתרו did.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about the meaning of ויחד יתרו
steps.stepSummary: רב says ויחד means יתרו passed a sharp knife over his flesh. שמואל says his whole flesh broke out in prickles.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the words 'ויחד יתרו', רב and שמואל disagree. רב says: he passed a sharp knife over his flesh. שמואל says: his whole body became covered in sharp prickles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the word ויחד in the פסוק right before יתרו's blessing. רב and שמואל each read it a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both readings connect ויחד to the root חד, meaning 'sharp'. רב understands it as a sharp knife, meaning יתרו cut himself through מילה and became a גר. שמואל understands it as sharp prickles on his skin, meaning יתרו felt pain when he heard that Egypt was destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: Usually read as 'and he rejoiced'; here it is linked to חַד, 'sharp'

steps.confusionAlert: Here ויחד is not read as the plain 'rejoiced'. רב and שמואל each explain the unusual word through the root חד, 'sharp', and each one ends up with a different picture.

phrases.english: 'ויחד יתרו' – רב and שמואל disagree.
phrases.notes: שמות 18:9, the פסוק just before יתרו's blessing.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: שֶׁהֶעֱבִיר חֶרֶב חַדָּה עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ,
phrases.english: רב says: that he passed a sharp sword over his flesh,
phrases.notes: He means that יתרו gave himself a ברית מילה and became a גר.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה חִדּוּדִים חִדּוּדִים כׇּל בְּשָׂרוֹ.
phrases.english: and שמואל says: that his whole flesh became covered in prickles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from יתרו's blessing to the word ויחד in the פסוק right before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: ויחד refers to מילה with a sharp knife. שמואל: ויחד means יתרו's skin prickled from distress.

steps.title: רב quotes a folk saying: do not insult gentiles in front of a convert
steps.stepSummary: רב says this matches the popular saying that you should not insult a non-Jew in front of a convert, even ten generations later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: This is what people say: With a convert, even up to ten generations, do not insult a gentile in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב connects שמואל's reading, that יתרו felt pain over Egypt, to a well-known saying people used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying explains why יתרו, who had joined Israel, still felt hurt when Egypt fell. A convert and his descendants can still feel close to where they came from. So one should be sensitive and not insult non-Jews in front of them.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (a folk saying)

phrases.english: רב said: This is what people say,
a convert, up to ten generations,
do not insult a non-Jew in front of him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links שמואל's reading in step 19 to a common saying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A convert stays sensitive to insults against non-Jews, even for generations, as יתרו's reaction shows.
steps.whatToRemember: ויחד יתרו is read through the root חד, 'sharp'. רב says it means מילה. שמואל says it means יתרו felt pain over Egypt, which fits the saying about not insulting non-Jews in front of a convert.

steps.title: What does במשמניו רזון mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about ה׳ sending 'leanness among his fat ones' and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Therefore the Master, ה׳ of hosts, will send leanness among his fat ones.' What does 'leanness among his fat ones' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by asking about the words במשמניו רזון in a פסוק about Assyria. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning is that Assyria's strong soldiers would grow weak. The גמרא is looking for a deeper reading of the unusual word משמניו.

keyTerms.meaning: His fat ones, his strong and healthy people

phrases.english: 'Therefore the Master, ה׳ of hosts, will send
leanness among his fat ones.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 10:16. The פסוק is about the punishment of Assyria.

phrases.english: What does 'leanness among his fat ones' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the fall of סנחריב.

steps.title: חזקיה, with eight names, will punish סנחריב, who has eight names
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: Let חזקיה, who has eight names, come and punish סנחריב, who also has eight names.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: Let חזקיהו, who has eight names, come and take revenge on סנחריב, who has eight names.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by reading משמניו as connected to שמונה, the number eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Through wordplay, משמניו becomes 'his eight'. סנחריב had eight names, and חזקיה, who also had eight names, would be the one to bring him down. The next steps list the names for each of them.

keyTerms.meaning: And he will take revenge, punish

phrases.english: הקדוש ברוך הוא said:

phrases.aramaic: יָבֹא חִזְקִיָּהוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁמוֹנָה שֵׁמוֹת,
phrases.english: Let חזקיהו, who has eight names, come,
phrases.notes: The word משמניו sounds like שמונה, eight. That's the wordplay here.

phrases.aramaic: וְיִפָּרַע מִסַּנְחֵרִיב שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁמוֹנָה שֵׁמוֹת.
phrases.english: and take revenge on סנחריב, who has eight names.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משמניו hints at שמונה: חזקיה, who had eight names, would punish סנחריב, who had eight names.

steps.title: The source for חזקיה's eight names
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה's eight names come from the פסוק 'פלא יועץ אל גבור אבי עד שר שלום'.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה, as it is written: 'For a child is born to us, a son is given to us, and the rule is on his shoulder, and his name is called פלא יועץ אל גבור אבי עד שר שלום.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that חזקיה had eight names by quoting a פסוק in ישעיהו about a child who was born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads this פסוק as being about חזקיה. The list of names at the end of the פסוק adds up to eight.

phrases.english: חזקיה, as it is written: 'For a child is born to us,
a son is given to us,
and the rule is on his shoulder,

phrases.aramaic: וַיִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ פֶּלֶא יוֹעֵץ אֵל גִּבּוֹר
phrases.english: and his name is called פלא, יועץ, אל, גבור,
אבי, עד, שר, שלום.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 9:5. Count them: פלא, יועץ, אל, גבור, אבי, עד, שר, שלום. That makes eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof for the first half of step 22.

steps.title: Isn't חזקיה itself another name?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if we count his names, isn't חזקיה a ninth name?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also the name 'חזקיה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the count of eight. His own name, חזקיה, should make nine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the eight titles from the פסוק are all names, then his everyday name should be counted too. That would break the match of eight against eight.

phrases.english: But there is also 'חזקיה'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count of eight names in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חזקיה had exactly eight names.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own name חזקיה would be a ninth name.

steps.title: חזקיה is a description, not one of the counted names
steps.stepSummary: The name חזקיה describes him: ה׳ strengthened him, or he strengthened Israel's bond with ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means that ה׳ strengthened him. Another explanation: 'חזקיה' means that he strengthened Israel's connection to their Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חזקיה is not counted because it is a description of what happened, not one of his given names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name is split into חזק and יה. The first explanation reads it as 'ה׳ made him strong'. The second reads it as 'he made Israel strong toward ה׳'. Either way, it is a title earned by his deeds, so the count stays at eight.

phrases.english: That ה׳ strengthened him.
Another explanation: 'חזקיה' –
that he strengthened Israel toward their Father in Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the name as a descriptive title
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיה looks like a ninth name.
steps.terutzMaskana: חזקיה is a description of strengthening, so it is not one of the eight names.

steps.title: The list of סנחריב's eight names
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists סנחריב's names found in the פסוקים: תגלת פלאסר, פלנאסר, שלמנאסר, פול, סרגון, אסנפר רבא ויקירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: סנחריב, as it is written about him: תגלת פלאסר, פלנאסר, שלמנאסר, פול, סרגון, and אסנפר the great and honored.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows the other half of the match: the eight names of סנחריב, collected from different places in תנ"ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these is the name of an Assyrian king found in a פסוק in תנ"ך. The גמרא treats all of them as names of סנחריב. To reach eight, matching חזקיה's eight, אסנפר, רבא and יקירא must each be counted as a separate name.

keyTerms.meaning: A name of an Assyrian king (מלכים ב 15:29)
A name of an Assyrian king (עזרא 4:10)

phrases.english: סנחריב, as it is written about him:
תגלת פלאסר, פלנאסר,
שלמנאסר, פול, סרגון,
אסנפר the great and honored.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof for the second half of step 22.

steps.title: Isn't סנחריב itself another name?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: isn't the name סנחריב an extra name beyond the eight?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also the name 'סנחריב'!
steps.whatsHappening: The same challenge as before, now about סנחריב: his best-known name would make the count more than eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all the listed names count, then סנחריב, the name used in the story itself, should count too. That would break the eight-to-eight match.

keyTerms.meaning: The king of Assyria who attacked ירושלים in the days of חזקיה

phrases.english: But there is also 'סנחריב'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same challenge as step 24, now applied to סנחריב's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that סנחריב had exactly eight names.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The name סנחריב itself would be an extra name.

steps.title: סנחריב is a description of his quarrelsome, arrogant speech
steps.stepSummary: The name סנחריב describes him: his talk was a fight, or he spoke arrogantly against ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means that his talk was a fight. Another explanation: that he spoke and spat out words against Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that סנחריב is not counted because it is a description of his behavior, not a real given name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name is split into parts. One reading is סיחתו ריב, 'his speech is a quarrel'. The other is סח ונחר, 'he spoke and snorted' against ה׳. Like חזקיה, it is a title based on his actions, so both kings stay at eight names.

keyTerms.meaning: That his speech was a quarrel
And he snorted, spat out (rude words)

steps.whatToRemember: במשמניו hints at שמונה: חזקיה had eight names and punished סנחריב, who also had eight. The names חזקיה and סנחריב are not counted, because each one describes the person's deeds. חזקיה strengthened and was strengthened, while סנחריב spoke with quarrel and arrogance.

phrases.english: That his speech was a quarrel.
Another explanation: that he spoke and snorted out
words against Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 27, the same way step 25 answered step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the name as a descriptive title
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סנחריב looks like an extra name.
steps.terutzMaskana: סנחריב describes his quarrelsome and arrogant speech, so it is not counted among the eight.

steps.title: Why סנחריב earned an honorable name
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says סנחריב was called 'אסנפר the great and noble' because he did not speak badly about ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why did that wicked man merit being called 'the great and noble אסנפר'? Because he did not speak badly about ארץ ישראל. The פסוק says he told the people, 'I will take you to a land like your land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The last name on the list, אסנפר רבא ויקירא, sounds like a compliment. רבי יוחנן explains why a wicked king deserved such a respectful name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When סנחריב tried to convince the Jews to go into exile, he only promised them a land 'like' theirs. He did not say his land was better. Because he did not put down ארץ ישראל, he was rewarded with an honorable title.

keyTerms.meaning: Spoke in disgrace of it, spoke badly about it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how much ארץ ישראל is valued: even a wicked enemy king is rewarded just for not speaking badly about it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
For what reason did that wicked one merit
to be called "the great and noble Asenappar"?
Because he did not speak
in disgrace of Eretz Yisrael,
as it is stated: "Until I come and take you
to a land like your land."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 18:32

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the honorable name אסנפר רבא ויקירא from the list of סנחריב's names in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סנחריב was rewarded with an honorable name because he did not speak badly about ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Was סנחריב clever or foolish?
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל argue: one says סנחריב was a clever king, the other says he was a foolish king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל disagree. One says he was a clever king, and the other says he was a foolish king.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל argue about how to judge סנחריב's words 'a land like your land.' This step only states the two opinions; the next steps explain each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on what סנחריב said. They disagree about whether saying it was smart or foolish. The גמרא does not say which אמורא holds which view.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel:
One says he was a clever king,
and one says he was a foolish king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks again at the words רבי יוחנן quoted and asks what kind of king says them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת whether סנחריב's promise showed cleverness or foolishness.

steps.title: Why the clever view calls him clever
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that he was clever, he knew that if he promised a better land, the people would call him a liar.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says he was a clever king, he thought: If I tell them 'it is better than your land,' they will say 'You are lying.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the 'clever king' opinion. סנחריב chose his words carefully so the people would believe him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knew ארץ ישראל was an excellent land. A promise of a 'better' land would sound fake, so he promised only an equal land, which sounded believable.

phrases.english: According to the one who says he was a clever king –
[he thought:] If I tell them "it is better than your land,"
phrases.notes: The words in brackets show the גמרא is speaking in סנחריב's voice, as if he were thinking it out.

phrases.english: they will say "You are lying."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first opinion from step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He was clever because a modest promise is more believable than an exaggerated one.

steps.title: Why the foolish view calls him foolish
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that he was foolish, promising only an equal land gave the people no reason to leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says he was a foolish king says: If so, what is so great about his offer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the 'foolish king' opinion. It asks why anyone would agree to leave home for a land that is only the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To convince people to go into exile, you have to offer them something better. A land 'just like yours' offers no gain, so his speech failed as persuasion and was foolish.

keyTerms.meaning: His greatness, the advantage of his offer

phrases.english: And the one who says he was a foolish king –
[says:] If so, what is his greatness?
phrases.notes: He means: what is the advantage of the offer? Why would anyone leave home for a land that is only the same?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר מֶלֶךְ טִיפֵּשׁ הָיָה – אִם כֵּן, מַאי רְבוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second opinion from step 30, in contrast to step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The effectiveness of סנחריב's promise of 'a land like your land'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An offer of something equal gives no reason to move, so the speech could not persuade anyone.

steps.title: Where were the tribes exiled to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where סנחריב exiled the tribes.
steps.simpleTranslation: To where did he exile them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple factual question: to which place did סנחריב send the exiled tribes? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only said 'a land like your land' without naming it. The גמרא wants to know the actual place.

phrases.english: To where did he exile them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what סנחריב promised to where he actually sent them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The location to which סנחריב exiled the tribes.

steps.title: Two answers about the place of exile
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says they were exiled to אפריקי; רבי חנינא says to הרי סלוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: to אפריקי. רבי חנינא said: to הרי סלוג.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question, each naming a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple disagreement about a historical fact. Each one names the land סנחריב called 'like your land.'

phrases.english: Mar Zutra says: To Afrikei,
and Rabbi Chanina says: To the Selug Mountains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Afrikei according to מר זוטרא; the Selug Mountains according to רבי חנינא.

steps.title: The exiles spoke badly about ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: Unlike סנחריב, the Jewish exiles did speak badly of ארץ ישראל, naming each place to show it was equal to or better than their land.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Jews spoke badly about ארץ ישראל. When they reached שוש, they said: 'It is equal to our land.' When they reached עלמין, they said: 'It is like our world.' When they reached שוש תרי, they said: 'For every one good thing there, there are two here.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא contrasts the exiles with סנחריב. He did not put down ארץ ישראל, but they did, and the names of the places show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each place name is a word-play on what they said. שוש sounds like 'equal,' עלמין means 'like our world' (ארץ ישראל), and שוש תרי sounds like 'two.' Each step goes further: equal, then the same as home, then twice as good.

keyTerms.meaning: Worlds; here, 'like our world,' meaning ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. סנחריב, the enemy, did NOT speak badly of ארץ ישראל. The Jewish exiles did.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sharp contrast is the point of the section: the Jews' own words were worse than the words of the wicked king.

phrases.english: But the Jewish people spoke
in disgrace of Eretz Yisrael.
When they arrived at Shosh,
they said: It is equal to our land.
phrases.notes: שוש sounds like שויא, which means equal.

phrases.english: When they arrived at Almin,
they said: It is like our world.
When they arrived at Shosh the second,
they said: For one, there are two.
phrases.notes: They meant: for every good thing in ארץ ישראל, this place has two.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל סִפְּרוּ בִּגְנוּתָהּ שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יוחנן's theme from step 29 and contrasts סנחריב with the exiles who arrived at these places.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exiles disgraced ארץ ישראל by praising their places of exile as equal or better.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: burned beneath his glory, not the glory itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about the burning of סנחריב's army, and רבי יוחנן says the fire burned beneath his 'glory,' not the glory itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And beneath his glory a blaze shall burn like the burning of fire.' רבי יוחנן said: beneath his glory, but not his actual glory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new פסוק about how סנחריב's army was destroyed. רבי יוחנן reads 'beneath his glory' carefully: the fire burned what was under the glory, not the glory itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what 'his glory' means. רבי יוחנן reads it as something on the outside, so the fire burned what was underneath it while the outside stayed whole. The next step shows what he means by 'glory.'

phrases.english: "And beneath his glory shall be kindled a blaze like the burning of fire."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 10:16. The פסוק has both words, יֵקַד יְקֹד, so the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Beneath his glory,
but not his actual glory.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the second half of the same פסוק (ישעיהו 10:16) expounded in step 21 and explains how סנחריב's army was destroyed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fire burned what was beneath the 'glory,' while the 'glory' itself stayed unburned.

steps.title: Clothing is called 'glory'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן used to call his clothes 'my glory,' which shows that 'glory' here means clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבי יוחנן did: he called his clothes 'the things that honor me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבי יוחנן's reading by showing that clothes are called 'glory.' So 'beneath his glory' means beneath their clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'glory' means clothing, the reading is clear: the fire burned the soldiers' bodies under their clothes, while the clothes stayed whole.

phrases.english: Like that practice of Rabbi Yochanan,
who would call his clothes "those that honor me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's reading in step 36 by defining 'glory' as clothing.
steps.raayaObject: That 'his glory' in the פסוק refers to clothing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's own habit of calling his clothes 'מכבדותי'.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the actual glory, like בני אהרן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says it means beneath his actual glory, like the burning of בני אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: beneath his actual glory, like the burning of the sons of אהרן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר disagrees with רבי יוחנן. He says 'glory' is meant literally, and he compares the death of סנחריב's army to the death of בני אהרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, 'glory' is not clothing. He reads 'beneath his glory' as the inner part, like the soul being burned, as happened to נדב and אביהוא. The next step spells out the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: The sons of אהרן (נדב and אביהוא)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
Beneath his actual glory,
like the burning of the sons of Aaron.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: תַּחַת כְּבוֹדוֹ מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same פסוק from step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'His glory' is meant literally, and the burning was like that of בני אהרן.

steps.title: Soul burned, body left whole
steps.stepSummary: Just as בני אהרן's souls were burned while their bodies stayed whole, so too סנחריב's army.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as there, the soul was burned and the body stayed whole, so too here, the soul was burned and the body stayed whole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי אלעזר's comparison. The army died the way בני אהרן did: their souls were burned out, but their bodies stayed whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains what 'beneath his actual glory' means for רבי אלעזר: the fire reached inside and took the soul, without burning the flesh. Both opinions agree something stayed whole on the outside. They differ on what: the clothes (רבי יוחנן) or the body itself (רבי אלעזר).

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there... so too here

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: the bodies burned beneath the clothes ('glory' = clothing). רבי אלעזר: the souls burned while the bodies stayed whole, like בני אהרן.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן שְׂרֵיפַת נְשָׁמָה וְגוּף קַיָּים,
phrases.english: Just as there, it was a burning of the soul and the body stayed whole,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the death of בני אהרן in ויקרא 10.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן שְׂרֵיפַת נְשָׁמָה וְגוּף קַיָּים.
phrases.english: so too here, it was a burning of the soul and the body stayed whole.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַלָּן שְׂרֵיפַת נְשָׁמָה וְגוּף קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the comparison to בני אהרן made in step 38.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי אלעזר, סנחריב's soldiers died with their souls burned and their bodies left whole, just like בני אהרן.

steps.title: פרעה blasphemed personally and was punished by ה׳ personally
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי יהושע בן קרחה teaches that פרעה insulted ה׳ himself, so ה׳ Himself punished him. It then begins to describe סנחריב, who also insulted ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי יהושע בן קרחה: פרעה, who insulted ה׳ himself, was punished by ה׳ Himself. סנחריב, who insulted ה׳...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a teaching that compares two kings who insulted ה׳, starting with פרעה. It is also setting up the second half of the comparison, about סנחריב, which continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is 'measure for measure': the way a person sins shapes the way he is punished. פרעה did the insulting himself, so ה׳ did the punishing Himself. Bringing in סנחריב tells us his case will be set against פרעה's, and this links back to the burning of his army in the earlier steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Himself, personally. It is used for both the sinner and for ה׳.

steps.confusionAlert: The word בְּעַצְמוֹ appears twice with two different subjects. The first time it means פרעה himself did the insulting. The second time it means ה׳ Himself did the punishing.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה:
phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha:
Pharaoh, who himself blasphemed,

phrases.aramaic: נִפְרַע הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִמֶּנּוּ בְּעַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, Himself exacted retribution from him.
Sennacherib, who blasphemed
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished yet. סנחריב's side of the comparison continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining how סנחריב's army was burned (steps 36-39), the גמרא brings a ברייתא that places סנחריב's punishment beside פרעה's to show a measure-for-measure pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who insults ה׳ personally, like פרעה, is punished by ה׳ personally. The case of סנחריב is introduced as the contrasting example.
